title: The 8 Levels of Silencing Your Phone
house: A bustling neon-lit metropolis made of organic skyscrapers, bustling subway lines, and damp concrete alleys where fruit and vegetable people rush to their shifts.
catchphrase: The number on your forehead never lies.
links: Level 1 strawberry notices Level 8's golden watch in the subway.
Level 2 lemon works at the neon café where Level 5 drops huge tips.
Level 4 avocado drops his keys near Level 7's expensive sports car.

levels.open_loop: What was the urgent emergency hidden behind the restricted caller ID on her screen?

gegenspieler.tat: Laughs loudly at her dead battery and throws her buzzing phone into a puddle.

levels.name: Ruby, 22, Intern
levels.story: 0 dollar on your forehead? Who let this strawberry into the subway anyway? Maybe she can scrub my toilets right after she finishes crying over her broken life. The 8 levels of panicking when your phone rings. Level 1. My phone buzzed three times with an unknown caller, and I slammed my finger onto the side button to silence it so fast the glass cracked into a million tiny dangerous pieces. I am Ruby, 22, intern at a failing marketing firm, making just 450 dollars a month while living in a cramped moldy closet under the stairs. That cheap plastic toy is disturbing everyone on the platform with its annoying vibration. I clutched my vibrating device tighter against my chest, terrified of what the bank was calling about after my second overdraft notice this week. Throw that garbage away before it ruins my morning commute, you absolute loser. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Leo, 25, Barista
levels.story: The bar owner walks up and publicly humiliates the young barista for being two minutes late, screaming at him in front of all customers, completely unaware that Leo secretly hacked the owner's offshore bank accounts yesterday and transferred every single penny into his own name. The 8 levels of panicking when your phone rings. Level 2. My phone started vibrating right inside my apron pocket while I was pouring oat milk, and I smashed the volume down button so hard the battery cover popped off onto the wet floor. I am Leo, 25, morning barista at the neon café, drowning in crushing student debt and overdue electric bills that keep piling up. Hurry up with that foam, kid, my time is worth more than your entire miserable weekly paycheck, so stop wasting my morning. My hands shook as milk spilled over the ceramic rim, staining the counter white and ruining my shift completely. Pick that up before you stain my expensive Italian loafers, peasant. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Max, 31, Courier
levels.story: The courier gets brutally knocked down by an accelerating luxury car on the open street, and the wealthy driver mocks him mercilessly without knowing that inside the crushed delivery package lies the official, irrevocable termination notice for the driver's own job. The 8 levels of panicking when your phone rings. Level 3. My phone started ringing with a blaring alarm tone, and I yanked it from the dashboard mount, hitting mute so hard the battery fell out onto the floor. I am Max, 31, package courier dodging crazy traffic in a worn-out helmet while trying to survive. Watch where you are going, you broke delivery rat, before I run you over completely. I gripped my handlebars until my knuckles turned white, my phone battery sitting dead in my pocket while rent was due. Another package you cannot afford to deliver, huh loser? You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Oliver, 29, Accountant
levels.story: The bookkeeper is ruthlessly humiliated in front of the entire team during the morning meeting, treated like dirt, completely oblivious to the fact that his private offshore bank account balance is currently ten times higher than the arrogant boss's entire net worth. The 8 levels of panicking when your phone rings. Level 4. My desk phone started screaming right during a quarterly review, and I slammed the receiver down onto the cradle before it could ring twice. I am Oliver, 29, junior accountant buried under endless spreadsheets and empty coffee cups. Your numbers are completely sloppy, Oliver, just like your pathetic salary and your useless life. My hands froze over my keyboard as my personal cell buzzed violently in my suit pocket with debt collectors. Fix this balance sheet by noon or find a new cardboard box to live in on the street. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Julian, 34, Senior Consultant
levels.story: The high-end consultant arrogantly dismisses the clumsy strawberry intern from Level 1, completely unaware that she is actually his secret half-sister seeking revenge for their abandoned family heritage. The 8 levels of panicking when your phone rings. Level 5. My phone started vibrating against the marble table during a high-stakes client dinner, and I silenced it instantly by placing it face down. I am Julian, 34, senior consultant living in a sleek glass penthouse with minimalist furniture and endless debt. Watch where you are going, you clumsy peasant, ruining my expensive dinner with your pathetic presence. I adjusted my silk tie, feeling a surge of annoyance at her incompetence while ignoring the family resemblance entirely. I am so sorry, my phone just would not stop ringing either with urgent business matters. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Victor, 41, Tech Founder
levels.story: The tech founder viciously mocks the struggling courier from Level 3 right on the bustling street, laughing at his poverty, but in the exact next fraction of a second, a catastrophic, secret system error completely wipes out his entire start-up empire. I am Victor, 41, tech startup founder driving a matte gray electric sports car through the financial district. I rolled down my tinted window halfway, staring at him with pure disdain and unmatched arrogance. Get that overpriced toy off the road before you crash it and ruin traffic. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Clara, 45, Executive Director
levels.story: The cold executive director fires the hardworking accountant from Level 4 with a ruthless, icy smile, completely unaware that out the window, her own luxurious mega-yacht is being seized by federal tax authorities at this very second. The 8 levels of panicking when your phone rings. Level 7. My encrypted phone started vibrating on my mahogany desk, and I swiped the silent mode switch without breaking eye contact with my board members. I am Clara, 45, executive director of a multi-billion dollar conglomerate housed in a crystal tower. These numbers do not add up, Director, your division is bleeding cash and you are finished. I leaned back in my leather chair, letting out a cold, amused sigh of absolute superiority. The board is calling for an immediate emergency audit on your accounts to strip your wealth. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Ezra, 52, Supreme Chancellor
levels.story: The supreme chancellor loses everything in a stunning, merciless twist of absolute poetic justice, stripped of his entire empire and forced to hand over every last penny to the humble strawberry intern from Level 1. The 8 levels of panicking when your phone rings. Level 8. My master console began blinking with incoming signals from all seven levels simultaneously, and I pressed the master silence override with a calm, terrifying smile. I am Ezra, 52, supreme chancellor of the fruit metropolis, watching everything from the highest spire in the clouds before my final fall. Please, Chancellor, my accounts have been frozen and every phone in my tower is ringing off the hook because I lost it all. I spun my executive chair around to face the panoramic window overlooking the sprawling neon metropolis crumbling below. The numbers only show what you have stolen, but they never show who you truly are in the end. Which topic should we reveal in the next sensational series of our fruit metropolis?
